leads.name: The Galenbeck Dance Linden (Luisenlinde)

location.address: Former Gutspark (manor park), Galenbeck, 17099 Friedland, Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, Germany

leads.access: Free and publicly accessible; local signage points the way to the tree in the former estate park, and the village's annual festival is held beneath it.
leads.transport: In the village of Galenbeck, Friedland municipality, Mecklenburg Lake District; reached by road, no rail station in the village.
leads.verify_notes: Single-tree-destination candidate (2026-08-31 exception): the only surviving dance linden (Tanzlinde) in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern and the only one in northern Germany per English Wikipedia, a real regional superlative rather than an invented one. Planted 1788 in the manor park in honour of Princess (later Queen) Louise of Mecklenburg-Strelitz, hence its other name 'Luisenlinde'; the estate is separately linked to Field Marshal Gebhard Leberecht von Bluecher, who was held there in 1760. Carries an octagonal timber dance platform about 3 metres above ground, rebuilt in 1993, holding room for about 24 people; crown pruned to its current rounded shape in 2002. Two independent sources agree closely: English Wikipedia (14m height, 234y as of 2022, so planted 1788) and baumkunde.de (last observed 11 Aug 2016, vital, girth 3.19m at that date, height 14.0m, age given as 240-250y). Girth recorded is baumkunde's own tape measurement; note it will have grown somewhat since 2016. Species given by baumkunde as 'Hollaendische Linde' (Dutch Lime), the German-language name for Tilia x europaea, matching Wikipedia's Tilia x europaea directly, so this is a settled species identification rather than a genus guess. Anecdote to lead with: a tree built INTO a dance floor, the last one of its kind left standing in the whole region.
